blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The downfall of the Mauryan Empire in 185 BC led to the rise of native dynasties like the Sungas, Kanvas, and Satavahanas, alongside foreign powers such as the Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Parthians, and Kushans.
Pushyamitra Sunga established the Sunga dynasty after overthrowing the last Mauryan ruler, Brihadratha, and performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice.
The Satavahana dynasty dominated the Deccan region, with Gautamiputra Satakarni restoring their power and promoting both Vedic traditions and Buddhist institutions.
Indo-Greek king Menander (Milinda) adopted Buddhism under the influence of philosopher Nagasena, as documented in the famous text 'Milindapanho'.
Kanishka, the most prominent Kushan ruler, convened the 4th Buddhist Council in Kundalavana (Kashmir), marking the formal division of Buddhism into Hinayana and Mahayana sects.

blocks.content: The Post-Mauryan Period marks an important transitional phase in ancient Indian history after the decline of the Mauryan Empire. This period witnessed political fragmentation, the rise of several regional powers, increased foreign contacts, and significant cultural, religious, and artistic developments. The Post-Mauryan Period roughly extends from 185 BC to around 300 AD.

After the death of Ashoka, the Mauryan Empire weakened due to inefficient successors, administrative over-centralization, and economic strain. The last Mauryan ruler, Brihadratha, was assassinated by his commander Pushyamitra Shunga, leading to the rise of the Shunga dynasty.
Pushyamitra Shunga founded the Shunga dynasty after killing the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha. He ruled from 185 BC to 149 BC and established his capital at Pataliputra.
The Shungas revived Brahmanical traditions and performed Ashvamedha Yajnas. They patronized Sanskrit learning and orthodox Hindu practices.
The Shunga period is known for the development of Buddhist art, especially the expansion of stupas such as Bharhut and Sanchi. Wooden architecture and railings were prominent features.
The Kanva dynasty succeeded the Shungas when Vasudeva Kanva assassinated the last Shunga ruler. The Kanvas ruled for a short period and continued Brahmanical traditions.
The Post-Mauryan period witnessed the assimilation of foreign dynasties into the Indian socio-cultural fabric alongside a unprecedented flourish in international maritime trade.
The Indo-Greeks were among the earliest foreign rulers to establish their control in north- western India. They introduced new coins, artistic styles, and cultural interactions.
Menander was the most famous Indo-Greek ruler. He embraced Buddhism after discussions with the Buddhist monk Nagasena, as recorded in the text Milindapanho.
The Shakas were Central Asian tribes who entered India and established several kingdoms. They introduced the Shaka Era beginning in 78 AD.
The Parthians ruled parts of north-western India and acted as intermediaries in Indo- Roman trade.

blocks.content: The Kushanas were originally a Central Asian tribe known as the Yueh-chi. They established a powerful empire covering Central Asia, Afghanistan, and northern India.
Kanishka was the greatest Kushana ruler. He patronized Buddhism and convened the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir. His reign marked the beginning of the Shaka Era according to some traditions.
Kushanas followed religious tolerance and patronized Buddhism, Hinduism, and Zoroastrianism. They played a key role in the spread of Mahayana Buddhism.
The Kushana period witnessed the development of Gandhara and Mathura schools of art. Gandhara art shows Greek influence, while Mathura art reflects indigenous Indian traditions.
The Satavahanas ruled the Deccan and were important contemporaries of the Kushanas. They promoted trade, issued coins, and supported Brahmanism and Buddhism.

items: Indo-Greeks were the first rulers in ancient India to issue gold coins and coins bearing the portraits and names of kings.
The Saka Era, starting in 78 AD under Kanishka's reign, serves as the basis for the official National Calendar of India.
Gautamiputra Satakarni is referred to as 'Eka Brahmana' (the unique Brahmana) in the famous Nasik Cave Inscription.
The 4th Buddhist Council was presided over by Vasumitra with Asvaghosa as his deputy during Kanishka's rule.

blocks.content: The Post-Mauryan period experienced significant growth in trade and commerce. Roman trade flourished, and gold coins became more common.
Urban centers developed further, guilds became powerful, and social stratification increased. Buddhism and Jainism continued to flourish.
This period saw progress in medicine, astronomy, and literature. Sanskrit and Prakrit literature expanded.
By the third century AD, most Post-Mauryan kingdoms declined due to internal weaknesses and external invasions, paving the way for the Gupta Empire.

Founder of Shunga dynasty – Pushyamitra Shunga. Indo-Greek ruler – Menander. Book Milindapanho – Dialogue between Menander and Nagasena. Great Kushana ruler – Kanishka. Gandhara art – Greek influence.
